problems.title: Binary Search
problems.titleHi: Binary Search - Sorted Array mein Dhundho

description.en: Given a sorted array of n integers and a target value, find the index of the target using Binary Search. If the target is not found, return -1.
description.hi: Ek sorted array diya hai n integers ka aur ek target value, Binary Search use karke target ka index dhundho. Agar target nahi milta toh -1 return karo.

explanation.en: 10 is not present in the array

constraints: Array is sorted in ascending order

hints.en: Compare target with middle element and eliminate half the search space each time
hints.hi: Target ko middle element se compare karo aur har baar aadhi search space eliminate karo

starterCode.python:
def binary_search(arr, target):
    # Write your code here
    return -1

n = int(input())
arr = list(map(int, input().split()))
target = int(input())
print(binary_search(arr, target))

approach.en: Use two pointers low and high. Compare target with mid element and halve search space.
approach.hi: Do pointers low aur high use karo. Target ko mid element se compare karo aur search space aadhi karo.

code.python:
def binary_search(arr, target):
    low, high = 0, len(arr) - 1
    while low <= high:
        mid = low + (high - low) // 2
        if arr[mid] == target: return mid
        elif arr[mid] < target: low = mid + 1
        else: high = mid - 1
    return -1

explanation.hi: 8 pehli baar index 3 pe aur aakhri baar index 4 pe hai

hints.en: Use Binary Search twice - once to find the first occurrence and once for the last
hints.hi: Binary Search do baar use karo - ek baar pehli occurrence ke liye aur ek baar aakhri ke liye

hints.hi: Pehli occurrence ke liye, jab arr[mid] == target, toh high = mid - 1 karo aur result store karo

problems.title: Find Peak Element

description.en: A peak element is an element that is strictly greater than its neighbors. Given an integer array, find any peak element and return its index. The array may contain multiple peaks; return the index of any one. Assume arr[-1] = arr[n] = -infinity.
description.hi: Peak element wo element hai jo apne dono neighbors se strictly bada hota hai. Ek integer array diya hai, koi bhi peak element dhundho aur uska index return karo. Array mein multiple peaks ho sakte hain; kisi bhi ek ka index return karo. Maan lo arr[-1] = arr[n] = -infinity.

explanation.en: 3 is a peak element at index 2 (3 > 2 and 3 > 1)
explanation.hi: 3 peak element hai index 2 pe (3 > 2 aur 3 > 1)

explanation.en: Either index 1 (element 2) or index 5 (element 6) is a valid answer

hints.hi: Binary Search: agar arr[mid] < arr[mid+1], toh peak right side pe hai

hints.hi: Bade neighbor wali side ki taraf jao

description.en: Write an efficient algorithm to search for a target value in an m x n matrix. The matrix has the following properties: each row is sorted in ascending order, and the first integer of each row is greater than the last integer of the previous row.
description.hi: Ek efficient algorithm likho jo m x n matrix mein target value dhundhe. Matrix ki properties: har row ascending order mein sorted hai, aur har row ka pehla integer pichli row ke aakhri integer se bada hai.

explanation.en: 3 is present in the matrix at position (0, 1)
13 is not present in the matrix

hints.en: Treat the 2D matrix as a flattened sorted 1D array and apply binary search
hints.hi: 2D matrix ko ek flat sorted 1D array ki tarah treat karo aur binary search lagao

hints.en: Map 1D index to 2D: row = mid / cols, col = mid % cols
hints.hi: 1D index ko 2D mein map karo: row = mid / cols, col = mid % cols

starterCode.python:

    # Write your code here
    return False

m, n = map(int, input().split())
matrix = []
for i in range(m):
    matrix.append(list(map(int, input().split())))
target = int(input())

approach.en: Treat 2D matrix as 1D sorted array. Use binary search with index mapping: row = mid/cols, col = mid%cols.
approach.hi: 2D matrix ko 1D sorted array samjho. Binary search use karo index mapping ke saath: row = mid/cols, col = mid%cols.

code.python:
def search_matrix(matrix, target):
    m, n = len(matrix), len(matrix[0])
    low, high = 0, m * n - 1
    while low <= high:
        mid = low + (high - low) // 2
        val = matrix[mid // n][mid % n]
        if val == target: return True
        elif val < target: low = mid + 1
        else: high = mid - 1
    return False

description.en:
Given an array of integers where arr[i] represents the number of pages in the i-th book, and m students, allocate books to m students such that:
1. Each student gets at least one book
2. Books are allocated in contiguous order
3. The maximum number of pages allocated to a student is minimized

Return the minimum possible value of the maximum pages.

2. Books contiguous order mein allocate ho
3. Kisi bhi student ko milne wale maximum pages minimize ho

Maximum pages ki minimum possible value return karo.

explanation.en: Allocation: [12, 34, 67] and [90]. Max pages = max(113, 90) = 113. This is the minimum possible maximum.

description.en: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of size m and n respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays. The overall run time complexity should be O(log(min(m, n))).
description.hi: Do sorted arrays diye hain nums1 aur nums2 jinke sizes m aur n hain, dono arrays ka combined median return karo. Overall time complexity O(log(min(m, n))) honi chahiye.

hints.en: Binary search on the smaller array to find the correct partition
hints.hi: Chhote array pe binary search karo sahi partition dhundhne ke liye

hints.en: Partition both arrays such that left half has (m+n+1)/2 elements and all left elements <= all right elements
hints.hi: Dono arrays ko aise partition karo ki left half mein (m+n+1)/2 elements ho aur saare left elements <= saare right elements
